facts.raw_span: A man in his 50s presented with new and progressive satellite lesions while undergoing pembrolizumab therapy
Two years earlier, he had undergone a wide local excision with graft repair for a left posterior auricular scalp lesion
An incidentally resected lymph node was found to be focally involved, with no evidence of distant metastatic disease
Multiple unresectable satellite lesions appeared
He received 4 cycles of ipilimumab, followed by a second wide local excision when new lesions appeared
Additional satellite lesions developed and he began pembrolizumab therapy, but after 5 cycles, local progression occurred in the satellite lesions
Multiple satellite lesions were present on the left posterior auricular scalp area
clinically regressed lesions with persistent black pigmentation were noted
H&E sections showed intense mixed superficial and deep dermal inflammatory infiltrate composed of numerous neutrophils, histiocytes, eosinophils, and lymphocytes
SOX-10 and MART-1: Highlighted normal melanocytes in basal layer of epidermis only
CD163 and myeloperoxidase: Highlighted histiocytes and neutrophils respectively
complete tumor regression and neutrophil-rich mixed inflammation; MART-1 immunostain confirms complete tumor regression

concepts.why: The patient has a history of melanoma, with an initial wide local excision and graft repair, and subsequent development of satellite lesions, which is consistent with melanoma.
The patient developed progressive satellite lesions while undergoing pembrolizumab therapy, which is an immune checkpoint inhibitor, suggesting an immune-related adverse reaction.
The patient's melanoma has progressed despite multiple treatments, including wide local excision, ipilimumab, and pembrolizumab, indicating treatment-resistant disease.
The patient developed an intense mixed inflammatory infiltrate while undergoing pembrolizumab therapy, which is consistent with an inflammatory reaction induced by the treatment.
The presence of histiocytes highlighted by CD163 immunostaining explains the uncovered fact of histiocytic infiltrate in the pathology report.

rationales.F01: New and progressive satellite lesions suggest melanoma progression
rationales.F03: Incidentally resected lymph node with focal involvement indicates early melanoma spread
rationales.F06: Local progression despite pembrolizumab therapy suggests treatment-resistant melanoma
rationales.F09: Intense mixed inflammatory infiltrate is consistent with immune-related adverse reaction and histiocytic infiltrate
rationales.F10: Normal melanocytes in basal layer of epidermis only, highlighted by SOX-10 and MART-1, indicate melanoma
rationales.F12: Complete tumor regression confirmed by MART-1 immunostain suggests successful treatment response

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of multiple unresectable satellite lesions, local progression despite pembrolizumab therapy, and evidence of complete tumor regression with subsequent recurrence support the diagnosis of treatment-resistant melanoma.
